title: Extract shared field validators
prompt:
accounts/signup.py and accounts/profile.py each have their own copy of the email, username and phone checks (signup has _clean_email/_clean_username/_clean_phone, profile does it inline in update_profile), and they will drift. Please move the validation into a new module accounts/validators.py with these functions:

- validate_email(value) -> str
- validate_username(value) -> str
- validate_phone(value) -> str
- validate_display_name(value) -> str (the display-name check that currently lives only in profile.py)

Each takes the raw string, returns the normalised value exactly as the current code produces it, and raises accounts.errors.ValidationError with .field set to "email", "username", "phone" or "display_name" for the same inputs the current code rejects. validate_phone("") raises like any other invalid phone; treating a blank phone as "clear it" stays in update_profile, and the required-field and password checks stay in register. RESERVED_USERNAMES should be defined once, in validators.py.

Then make signup.register and profile.update_profile use these functions instead of their own copies, and delete signup's _clean_* helpers. Other code mocks these validators with unittest.mock.patch, so look them up when the call happens: either through the module (validators.validate_email(...)) or via names imported into signup/profile, but not captured in a dict or default argument at import time.

register and update_profile must behave exactly as before, including which field a ValidationError names. The tests in tests/ should keep passing.
acceptance: validators.py functions normalise and reject like the original code (email domains, username charset/length/reserved, phone separators/plus/length/ASCII digits, display-name whitespace/length/control chars) with the right .field; RESERVED_USERNAMES in validators; register and update_profile call the shared validators (verified by patching) and signup's _clean_* helpers are gone; register/update_profile outputs and error fields unchanged.
difficulty_rationale: Four files, two differently written copies of the same rules to reconcile without changing behaviour.
